After a run I cannot stop sweating for what seems like an hour or more. I sweat enough to make my shirts damp and have sweat rolling off my forehead. I live in Georgia (USA) so its pretty hot and humid in the afternoon but even if I run on my treadmill its the same story. I work inside so I am in the AC the whole time. I have tried cooling off for 15-20 minutes before getting in the shower, taking super cold showers, eating ice cream and drinking lots of cold water. Nothing seems to help me stop sweating and I am wondering if its normal to sweat this much for so long?
How long does it take you to stop sweating after a run?

It depends mainly on the weather. Summers are the worst - with temperatures around 30-35°C I feel like I'm melting for about half an hour after the run. Winters, on the other hand, are cool (pun intended). I stop sweating almost immediately when the temperature outside is below 0°C.

I run outside in the mornings/evenings when it's cool, and when I get home I stretch and then hop in the shower, so I'm not sure how long I sweat. Sometimes I sweat a little bit after my shower, but usually I don't. I'm also one of those people whose faces turn bright red from running so instead of sweating, I'm bright red for about half an hour.

I wouldn't worry about how much you're sweating as long as you're staying hydrated before, during, and after your workout, but you could always consult your doctor.
